channel.title: Bentonville Daily
channel.description: Public records and local institutions, daily.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 15, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville road closures for infrastructure work have been extended.
Bentonville road closures extended. Two road closures in Bentonville, accommodating infrastructure work, have been extended.
Bentonville city council briefed on Morning Star Schoolhouse renovation. The Bentonville City Council received an update on the ongoing renovation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse. The city anticipates the project will conclude in the spring.
Bentonville Bike Fest moves to September for 2027. The Bentonville Bike Fest will move to September for its 2027 event. Organizers hope the new dates will provide more favorable weather conditions.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event is scheduled for October 17, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale.
J.B. Hunt to release third quarter earnings. J.B. Hunt is scheduled to release the firm’s third quarter earnings.
Crystal bridges symposium to examine Indigenous art legacy. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host a symposium on October 16-17. The event will focus on the legacy of Indigenous art.
Silver house community darkroom opens in Springdale. Silver House, a community darkroom for film photographers, has found a home in Springdale. The space will serve as a creative hub for developing pictures and artistic experimentation.
Immerse Arkansas receives $4.5 million for new campus. Immerse Arkansas, a Little Rock-based nonprofit, received a $4.5 million anonymous gift and a 99-year land lease. This funding will establish short-term housing and a campus in Fayetteville.
Fayetteville municipal annex renamed for former mayor. The Fayetteville Municipal Annex has been renamed to honor a former mayor.
Fayetteville to host tenant toolkit event. The City of Fayetteville is inviting renters to a Tenant Toolkit event. The event will provide information on tenant rights, responsibilities, and lease signing.
SoNA Beyond music series begins with 11 concerts. The Symphony of Northwest Arkansas (SoNA) announced its sixth annual SoNA Beyond music series. The series will feature 11 free performances across the region, starting this month.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a wider variety of building types beyond single-family homes at 501 N Main Street, potentially increasing density and changing the character of the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to discuss bylaws for the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Advisory Board. This discussion would review the rules governing the members, terms, attendance, and officer elections for the Tree and Landscape Advisory Board, which could affect how the board operates and makes decisions.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed amendments could change the rules and regulations that govern development and land use throughout Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville City Council approved a rezoning request for 405 N.W. Fifth St. and accepted a $100,000 grant for library improvements.
Bentonville City Council approves Northwest Fifth street rezoning. The Bentonville City Council approved a second request to rezone 405 N.W. Fifth St., after denying a previous request for the same property last month.
Bentonville Public library to receive $100,000 grant. The Bentonville City Council voted to accept a $100,000 grant from Project for Public Spaces for future library improvement projects.
Rogers City Council accepts $500,000 in infrastructure grants. The Rogers City Council approved the acceptance of over $500,000 in grant funds from the Northwest Arkansas Regional Planning Commission for infrastructure projects.
Bentonville City Council approves land acquisition for infrastructure projects. The Bentonville City Council approved the land acquisition process for three planned road projects, allowing them to progress.
Northwest Arkansas commercial vacancy rates remain low. A new quarterly market summary by Cushman & Wakefield | Sage Partners indicates that the commercial real estate market in Northwest Arkansas, including office, industrial, and retail space, remains tight despite ongoing new construction.
Concerns raised over Northwest Arkansas development and utility coordination. Regional utility providers, planners, and developers have expressed concerns that the pace of development in Northwest Arkansas is outpacing the ability of cities and utility providers to coordinate infrastructure with new projects.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Washington regional expands Infusion Center capacity. Washington Regional Medical Center announced the expansion of its Infusion Center at the Fayetteville campus, which will triple its capacity and aim to improve the patient care experience.
Bentonville school bus drivers report fewer 'red-light runners'. Officials note a decrease in violations of school bus safety laws, though some problem areas persist across the Bentonville School District.
Rogers Public library to host lunch and learn on Northwest Arkansas baseball history. Education Manager Ashley Sayers from the Rogers Historical Museum will lead a program focusing on the local history of baseball as part of the Rogers Public Library's Lunch and Learn series.
Matchbox Twenty to perform at Walmart AMP in 2027. Rock band Matchbox Twenty is scheduled to perform at the Walmart AMP as part of the venue's expanding 2027 concert schedule.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale businesses at 501 N Main Street, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to review its operating bylaws. This item would update the rules for how the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Advisory Board operates, including member terms and attendance requirements as stipulated by City Ordinance No. 98-90.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed amendments could change various rules and regulations that affect development, land use, and other aspects of living and working in Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 13, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will extend the closure of Southwest A Street for ongoing sewer main extension work.
Bentonville extends southwest a street closure. The city of Bentonville has extended the closure of Southwest A Street as crews continue work on a sewer main extension.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 3006 SE J St from Town Center High to Neighborhood Node. This proposed change would alter the zoning classification of the property at 3006 SE J St, potentially affecting the density and type of development allowed there.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to approve a grant for design and environmental phases of improvements to the 1st Street and Pleasant Grove Road intersection. This would allow the city to receive a $133,600.00 grant and appropriate an additional $33,400.00 from street fund reserves to begin planning for improvements at the intersection of 1st Street and Pleasant Grove Road.
On the Bentonville Schools Board of Education agenda: Board to welcome attendees and call the meeting to order. This is a routine procedural step to begin the meeting, including the Pledge of Allegiance and roll call of board members.
Crystal Bridges opens all-ages playground. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art has opened a new play area, the Ozark Discovery Canopy, located between its Campus Parking Plaza and the museum in Bentonville.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Sam's Club member's mark community reaches 200,000 users. Sam's Club's member-based online community, Member's Mark Community, has surpassed 200,000 users, according to Executive Vice President and Chief Merchandiser Myron Frazier.
Walmart hosts community pet event. A community pet event was held on the Walmart Campus Welcome Lawn, featuring adoptable pets and highlighting the Cats as Therapy Project.
Illinois River offers good flow and fishing. Arkansas Game and Fish Commission fisheries staff are evaluating the sportfish population in the Illinois River from the Arkansas 16 bridge at Savoy to the Arkansas 59 bridge near the Oklahoma border.
NWA fishing report suggests trolling for crappie and walleye. The Northwest Arkansas fishing report, compiled by Flip Putthoff, suggests trolling as a good tactic for catching crappie and walleye.
NWA outdoor events include fall hike. The Hill 'n Dale Hiking Club will hike Crack in the Rock Trail, Teardrop Falls, and Homestead Trail near Van Buren and Lee Creek Reservoir at 9 a.m. Thursday.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 12, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has reissued a countywide 24-hour burn ban.
Benton County reissues burn ban. Benton County has issued a countywide 24-hour burn ban, re-establishing restrictions after two weeks of loosened regulations.
Benton County fire marshal issues burn ban. The Benton County Fire Marshal has issued a countywide 24-hour burn ban, prohibiting all outdoor, open burning.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Centerton City Council members vie for mayor seat. Centerton City Council members Wendy Henson and Cliff Thompson are competing to become the city's next mayor, discussing infrastructure and residents.
Chick-fil-A donates cookie sales to food banks. Participating Chick-fil-A restaurants in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley are partnering with local food banks this week, donating $1 from every 6-count Chocolate Chunk Cookie sold to address food insecurity.
Tyson Foods gives $100,000 to University of Arkansas-Pine Bluff. Tyson Foods is investing $100,000 in the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff to support career readiness and workforce development programs for college and high school students in the Arkansas Delta.
Benton County Fairgrounds hosts Vintage Market Days. Vintage Market Days of Northwest Arkansas returned to the Benton County Fairgrounds this weekend, featuring over 175 vendors for shopping, food, live music, and family activities.
Ozarks electric crew assists storm restoration in Alabama. A crew from Ozarks Electric headed to Alabama early Sunday morning to assist with emergency power restoration efforts in areas affected by Hurricane Isaias.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 11, 2026
item.description:
A mountain-bike race, Little Sugar MTB, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. It will be part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Bella Vista to open Razorback Greenway extension. Bella Vista will cut the ribbon on an extension of the Razorback Greenway by the end of the month. This follows improvements to a Bentonville trail.
Linemen to deploy to Mobile, Alabama, for hurricane relief. Northwest Arkansas linemen will deploy to Mobile, Alabama, by early Sunday to support hurricane relief efforts. They will join Baldwin EMC.
Immerse Arkansas receives donation for Fayetteville housing. Nonprofit Immerse Arkansas plans to bring short-term housing to Fayetteville for young adults in crisis. This follows a $4.5 million anonymous donation and a 99-year land lease from New Heights Church.
Fayetteville architect appointed to Achieve Community Alliance board. A Fayetteville-based architect was appointed to the Achieve Community Alliance board. This was among recent announcements of new hires, promotions, and awards from companies and organizations in Northwest Arkansas.
Springdale hosts fifth annual family history conference. Springdale hosted the fifth annual Bridging the Generations Family History Conference on October 9-10. The event invited locals to learn about their family history.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 10, 2026
item.description:
Bella Vista City Council is considering an ordinance to require council approval for automated license plate readers.
Bella Vista City Council considers ordinance for automated license plate readers. The Bella Vista City Council is considering an ordinance that would require council approval for the use of automated license plate readers in the city.
United Petfood acquires Benton County plant for $24.22 million. United Petfood, a private-label pet food manufacturer based in Belgium, acquired a 98,063-square-foot dry pet food plant in Decatur for $24.22 million. This purchase expands the company's North American footprint.
Manufacturing accelerator concludes in Bentonville. The Reel Advanced Manufacturing Program, a manufacturing accelerator, held a graduation ceremony in Bentonville for its inaugural class of 25 Arkansas manufacturers.
Walmart opens new fulfillment center in stockton, California. Walmart announced the opening of a more than 900,000-square-foot 'next-generation' fulfillment center in Stockton, California. This is the fifth such center opened by Walmart in California.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Northwest Arkansas Council discusses education and employment connections. Over 100 education and business leaders attended a panel and strategic plan presentation in Fayetteville from the Northwest Arkansas Council. The discussion focused on connections between education and regional employment opportunities.
Springdale golf tournament raises $180,000 for Jones center. A golf tournament held earlier this week in Springdale raised $180,000. The funds will help increase access to the Jones Center, a Northwest Arkansas community center.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 9, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will see two weeks of street closures on SW D Street starting next week.
SW D Street in Bentonville to close for two weeks. Multiple blocks of SW D Street in Bentonville will close during late morning and early afternoon hours for two weeks, beginning next week.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 3006 SE J St from Town Center High to Neighborhood Node. This proposed change would alter the zoning classification of the property at 3006 SE J St from T5.2, Town Center High to T4.2, Neighborhood Node, which could affect the types of buildings and businesses allowed there.
On the Bentonville Schools Board of Education agenda: Board to approve the meeting agenda. This is a routine step to formally adopt the list of items the Board will discuss and vote on during the meeting.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept a $6,683,590.00 grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main. This resolution would accept a grant of up to $6,683,590.00 from the Walton Family Foundation to help fund the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension, which could improve water infrastructure in the city.
Toys R Us to open store in Northwest Arkansas mall. Toys R Us will open a new store in the Northwest Arkansas Mall.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Bentonville Finance Committee to meet October 13. The City of Bentonville Finance Committee will hold a meeting on October 13, 2026, from 5:00 PM to 5:30 PM.
Rogers Executive Airport named Airport of the Year. The Rogers Executive Airport received the Airport of the Year Award from the Arkansas Department of Commerce, Division of Aeronautics.
Leon Bridges added to Walmart AMP 2027 schedule. Grammy award-winning singer and songwriter Leon Bridges has been added to the Walmart AMP's growing 2027 schedule.
Fayetteville apartments reopen as condos after renovation. Wilson Park Apartments have reopened as The Wilson Parkview Condos after a renovation by Fayetteville-based CJC Development.
LatinXNA economic summit scheduled in Northwest Arkansas. Serve2Perform is holding a LatinXNA Economic Summit in Northwest Arkansas in a few weeks.
Arkansas State School Board meets in Springdale. The Arkansas State School Board held a meeting at Bernice Young Elementary School in Springdale, which served as Capital for a Day.
George’s co-CEOs join Legacy Bank board. Carl George and Charles George, co-CEOs of George's, have been appointed to the Board of Directors for Springdale-based Legacy Bank.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 8, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville Planning Commission approved site plan elements for a Health Care Campus and an Institute of Technology.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves site plan elements for Health care campus and institute of technology. The Bentonville Planning Commission approved permit elements for two major construction projects: a Health Care Campus and an Institute of Technology.
Rogers voters to consider $8.75 million for animal services facility. Rogers voters will have the opportunity in November to support an $8.75 million animal services facility by extending an existing 1% sales tax.
Bentonville offers document shredding and device recycling. The City of Bentonville will offer residents an opportunity to dispose of electronic devices and important documents on Tuesday, October 13, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Rogers unveils Oakdale Middle School renovations. Rogers unveiled upgrades to Oakdale Middle School at a ribbon-cutting ceremony, marking the reopening of the school after a three-year renovation.
Arkansas Children’s Northwest completes $82.7 million expansion. Arkansas Children’s Northwest in Springdale completed an $82.7 million expansion, adding 15 inpatient beds and 50,000 square feet of new space, and renovating 23,000 square feet.
Community Clinic awarded $3 million federal grant. Springdale-based healthcare provider Community Clinic will receive $3 million from the Health Resources and Services Administration to expand rural substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery services.
Walmart hosts 125 prospective suppliers at Open Call event. Walmart's Open Call event hosted 125 prospective suppliers from 35 states and Puerto Rico at Sam Walton Hall on its Bentonville home office campus.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on airport engineering and construction projects. Residents would be interested in the progress of projects like the East Taxiway Extension, Hangar Access Road, East Parking Apron, West Taxiway Rehabilitation, West Turf Apron, Perimeter Fence Installation – Phase 1, and West Taxiway Extension, which are funded by the FAA, ADA, and BIL.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Review of September budget report. The body will review the financial status and expenditures of the museum for the month of September.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on various city airport matters. This includes highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, an update on Eastside Hangar Development, discussion of Airport Board Candidate Selection, and information regarding the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 7, 2026
item.description:
Bella Vista city offices will close Friday for a water-related construction project.
Bella Vista city offices to close Friday. Bella Vista city offices at the Town Center complex will be closed to the public on Friday due to a water-related construction project.
On the Bentonville Library Advisory Board agenda: Library to prioritize resources compatible with existing hardware and software. This item outlines the criteria the library would use when acquiring new resources, considering compatibility with current systems, licensing, and network access, ideally allowing access beyond the physical library building.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on various city and airport matters. This item includes updates on the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, Eastside Hangar Development, Airport Board Candidate Selection, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract, which could impact the airport's future development and governance.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Review of September budget report. The body will review the financial report for the museum's budget during the month of September.
Fayetteville city council prohibits city funds for license plate readers. The Fayetteville City Council voted to prohibit the use of city funds and property for automatic license plate readers, such as those distributed by Flock Safety.
Fayetteville city council bans city funds for license plate readers. The Fayetteville City Council voted to ban the use of city funds to purchase automatic license plate reader systems.
Crystal Bridges to open new outdoor playscape. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will open a new outdoor playscape next week.
Arkansas Children's Northwest unveils hospital expansion. Arkansas Children's Northwest celebrated the grand opening of its expanded Walker Campus in Springdale.
Onyx Coffee Lab named first business for Fayetteville's Drake Farms. Onyx Coffee Lab is the first commercial tenant at Fayetteville's Drake Farms, a large multiuse project on about 165 acres.
Swarm Aero unveils drone mock-up. Oxnard, California-based drone company Swarm Aero released a full-scale mock-up of a drone it might produce in Fayetteville.
Fayetteville site to build Swarm Aero Gamera drone. Swarm Aero, a developer of uncrewed aerial systems with an advanced manufacturing site in Northwest Arkansas, announced plans to introduce a new category of drone with global reach and lower costs.
Pea Ridge residential property sells for $8.08 million. A 100-lot residential property in Pea Ridge recently changed hands for $8.08 million, with the purchase price equaling $80,850 per lot.
WealthPath managed assets exceed $2 billion. The top-ranked locally-owned independent wealth management firms in Northwest Arkansas have exceeded $2 billion in managed assets.
Springdale clinic awarded $3 million grant. Community Clinic in Springdale was awarded a $3 million grant from the Health Resources and Services Administration to expand substance use disorder treatment in rural communities.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 5, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will have a road closure and lane reduction on Wednesday.
Bentonville schedules road closure and lane reduction for Wednesday. The city of Bentonville announced a lane reduction and road closure will take place on Wednesday.
Bentonville to host Dress for success gala on November 7. Dress for Success Northwest Arkansas will hold its annual Little Black Dress Gala on November 7 in Bentonville. The event will include an evening of glamour, celebration, and fundraising to support economic opportunity.
Bentonville to host Little Sugar MTB race on October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to accept a grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. The board is asked to accept a grant from the Walton Family Foundation of up to $6,683,590.00 to help fund the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. This project would expand the city's water supply infrastructure.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from single-family to neighborhood node. This change would allow for a mix of uses, potentially including small-scale commercial or multi-family housing, in an area currently designated for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and what recommendations it can make to the City Council, and may include the election of officers.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates from the city of Bentonville. This item would inform residents about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection process for an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Review of September budget report. The board will review the financial budget report for the museum for the month of September.
Rogers to hold fall tree giveaway on October 24. The city of Rogers will host a tree giveaway through its Foresting the Future program on October 24.
Rogers museum commission to meet on October 8. The Rogers Museum Commission will hold a meeting on October 8, from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM, at 313 S. 2nd Street.
Frozen berries recalled in Arkansas due to potential e. coli contamination. Frozen berries sold at Walmart and Trader Joe's stores in 30 states, including Arkansas, have been recalled by officials due to potential E. coli contamination.
Pea Ridge Library offers new telescope for public use. The Pea Ridge Community Library now has a telescope available for borrowing, allowing residents to view stars, planets, and galaxies with greater clarity.
Northwest Arkansas Business Journal announces 2026 C-Suite Award winners. The Northwest Arkansas Business Journal has announced its 12th class of C-Suite Award winners, recognizing top executives from various sectors.
Brad Sikorski spearheads McAuley Place construction in Bentonville. Brad Sikorski has led the construction of McAuley Place in Bentonville, a project that will provide affordable housing solutions in Northwest Arkansas.
Alison Nation leads Visit bentonville's digital engagement growth. Alison Nation's leadership at Visit Bentonville has resulted in increased digital engagement and visibility for the city.
Tom Allen involved in Pinnacle Hills area development in Rogers. Tom Allen has been involved in the development of the Pinnacle Hills area of Rogers, including leading development and leasing efforts for The Visionaries, Hunt Ventures’.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 3, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Institute of Technology broke ground on its approximately 444,000-square-foot campus at the former Walmart Home Office site.
Bentonville Institute of Technology breaks ground on new campus. Members of the Walton family and over 200 attendees were present at the groundbreaking ceremony for the approximately 444,000-square-foot Bentonville Institute of Technology, located at the former Walmart Home Office.
Bentonville announces downtown street closures. The city of Bentonville provided updates on two street closures near downtown.
Bentonville to host fall tree giveaway. The City of Bentonville will host a Fall Tree Giveaway on October 10, 2026, from 7:30 AM to 10:00 AM at 3200 SW Municipal Dr.
Bentonville Bike Fest to return in 2027. The Bentonville Bike Fest has announced its return in 2027.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Bentonville west defeats Springdale 35-9. Bentonville West secured a 35-9 victory over Springdale, with their offense scoring points early in the game.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to accept a grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. The board is asked to accept a grant from the Walton Family Foundation of up to $6,683,590.00 to help pay for the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. This would require a budget adjustment.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and potentially some small-scale commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what issues the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can address and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how local traffic and signage concerns are handled.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on city airport matters. The board would be informed about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection of an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Museum to present its September budget report. This report would provide an overview of the museum's financial status and spending for the month of September.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 2, 2026
item.description:
The Emerald, a $45.1 million multifamily development, has begun construction in Centerton.
Construction begins on $45.1 million multifamily project in Centerton. Capstone Building Corp. has started construction on The Emerald, a 256-unit, 312,414-square-foot multifamily development in Centerton.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how traffic and signage issues are addressed in the city.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on various city airport matters. This item would inform residents about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection process for an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
Walmart recalls 4.4 million grill brushes. Walmart has announced the recall of more than 4.4 million Expert Grill brushes due to an ingestion hazard, according to the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
Walmart pasta recall expanded for possible listeria contamination. A recall on pasta sold at Walmart locations nationwide has been expanded due to possible listeria contamination, according to a notice from the Food and Drug Administration.
Centerton to host forum for mayoral and City Council candidates. A candidate forum will be held in Centerton for those running for mayor and City Council.
Siloam springs launches multifamily recycling program. A recent grant will enable Siloam Springs to deploy a new multifamily recycling program.
Northwest Arkansas Community College to host inaugural homecoming festivities. Northwest Arkansas Community College will celebrate its first-ever homecoming, with college officials hoping for a strong start.
Educators discuss early technical training at Bentonville summit. At a Bentonville summit, educators highlighted the importance of early technical training and workforce preparation, noting a shortage of workers in skilled trades.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust names Marson Nance as new CEO. Marson Nance, a longtime conservation leader, has been named the new CEO of the Northwest Arkansas Land Trust.
Red clay strays added to 2027 Walmart AMP schedule. The Alabama-based country rock band Red Clay Strays has announced new tour dates for 2027, including a stop at the Walmart AMP.
September 2026 was warmest on record for Northwest Arkansas. September 2026 was the warmest September on record for Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley, with temperatures significantly exceeding historical averages.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 1, 2026
item.description:
The Willard & Pat Walker Charitable Foundation donated $15 million to Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art to provide free admission to temporary exhibitions.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and potentially some small-scale commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can do, including electing officers and making recommendations to the City Council.
Bella Vista to offer free fall trees with sign-up beginning Friday. Bella Vista residents can sign up starting this week to receive a free tree later this month.
Bikes, Blues and BBQ begins in Rogers. The Bikes, Blues and BBQ event kicked off in Rogers on Wednesday night.
Crystal Bridges receives $15 million for free temporary exhibit admission. The Willard & Pat Walker Charitable Foundation donated $15 million to Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art to provide free admission to its temporary exhibitions for visitors 25 and younger, veterans, active-duty military, and SNAP recipients.
Benton County opens new justice center. A new justice center is now operational in Benton County.
SGS bicycle testing company earns Bentonville accreditation. SGS, a bicycle testing company, has received accreditation for its Bentonville lab.
Walmart awards $15 million grant to feeding America. Walmart has awarded a $15 million grant to the Feeding America nonprofit organization.
Scouting America council to honor Hunt family. The Natural State Council of Scouting America will honor the Hunt family at its 2026 Northwest Arkansas Heart of the Eagle luncheon.
Jobless rates decline in most Arkansas metros. Jobless rates in August were lower in six of the seven metro areas in or connected to Arkansas compared with August 2025, with Northwest Arkansas having the lowest rate at 2.9%.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust CEO Grady Spann retires. Grady Spann, CEO and executive director of the Northwest Arkansas Land Trust, will retire on October 1, and Marson Nance has been promoted to succeed him.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 30, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court has begun its 2027 budget process.
Benton County Quorum Court begins 2027 budget process. The Benton County Quorum Court has started planning for the 2027 fiscal year by reviewing forecasted finances and departmental needs.
Rogers announces road closures for Bikes, Blues & BBQ. The city of Rogers is warning motorists about street closures and traffic changes this week due to the annual Bikes, Blues & BBQ event.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of residential and commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, potentially bringing more services or housing options to the area.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee is responsible for, including the election of officers and potential recommendations to the City Council.
Calara working on $565 million in Benton County housing projects. Calara, the land development arm of Rausch Companies, is under contract for a Bentonville land deal that would create approximately 900 residential lots, part of an estimated $565 million in housing projects in Benton County.
Chamber of mothers expands into Arkansas with new chapters. Chamber of Mothers, a nonpartisan nonprofit focused on maternal health, affordable childcare, and paid leave, has launched chapters in Northwest Arkansas and Little Rock.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Bentonville medical center offers free mammograms. Bentonville Medical Center is partnering with a local breast cancer nonprofit to offer free screenings this week.
Washington County judge candidates debate in Springdale. Candidates for Washington County judge participated in a debate in Springdale, discussing population growth and infrastructure.
University Auto And Tire opens second location in Elkins. Fayetteville-based University Auto and Tire has opened its second location in Elkins after acquiring a 6,500-square-foot vehicle maintenance shop.
Perrodin Supply Co. announces artists for Spring Creek exhibition. Perrodin Supply Co. has announced the artists who will be featured in its month-long exhibition celebrating Springdale's Spring Creek.
Rogers to host garden alchemy: herbs for home & Well-Being event. The city of Rogers will host a 'Garden Alchemy: Herbs for Home & Well-Being' event on October 10, exploring Victorian herbs.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 29, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will celebrate the grand opening of a new trail tunnel near the Walmart Campus this week.
Bentonville to open new trail tunnel. The city of Bentonville will cut the ribbon this week on a new trail tunnel near the Walmart Campus, following multiple years of construction.
Square 2 Square Bike Ride returns to Bentonville. The Square 2 Square Bike Ride will conclude in downtown Bentonville this fall, marking its first return since 2023.
Square 2 Square bike ride to use Razorback Greenway on October 3. The Square 2 Square bike ride will take place on the Razorback Greenway on October 3, connecting Downtown Fayetteville and Downtown Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how traffic and signage issues are addressed in the city.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Lowell daycare site sells for $9.3 million. A 40,000-square-foot daycare building in Lowell, located near Interstate 49, recently sold for $9.3 million.
Rogers apartment complex sells for $51.85 million. The Fitzroy Grove, a 250-unit luxury apartment complex east of Interstate 49 in Rogers, recently sold for $51.85 million.
Bentonville housing development targets teacher needs. McAuley Place, a new housing development in Bentonville, is designed to help teachers afford to live in the area and save for homeownership.
Bentonville remains first in Arkansas Sports Media Poll. The Bentonville Tigers maintained their unbeaten record and top position in the latest Arkansas Sports Media Poll.
UA power group launches as new research institute. The University of Arkansas officially launched a new overarching research institute for electronics systems on Monday.
Walmart AMP seeks collector ticket designs. The Walmart AMP is holding a contest for collector ticket designs for its 2027 season.
Child care aware of NWA discusses early childhood education. A nonprofit organization, Child Care Aware of NWA, brought together advocates and providers to discuss solutions for childcare access in Arkansas.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 28, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has lifted its burn ban, which had been in effect since August.
Benton County lifts burn ban. Benton County's fire marshal has lifted the county's burn ban, which had been active since August.
Tractor Supply Co. and freddy’s frozen custard & steakburgers to open in lowell. Lowell is set to gain a new fast food restaurant and a Tractor Supply Co. following the approval of development plans last week.
New affordable apartment complex opens in Bentonville. A new workforce housing community officially opened its doors in Bentonville on September 25.
Bienvenue Restaurant moves to Pinnacle Hills. Bienvenue Restaurant, a European-inspired establishment, recently opened in the former Theo’s Rogers location at 3300 S. Market Street, Suite 100, in Rogers.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would cut the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%, potentially making dining out slightly less expensive.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider splitting a lot at 44 Watson Drive. This proposed lot split, Case LSP-2026-67100, would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 into multiple parcels. The applicant is Troy Currens.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve buying a new John Deere tractor for the Street Department. This resolution would authorize the purchase of a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for $63,860.36, which the Street Department would use for maintenance.
Harps Food Stores announces promotions. Will McDoniel has been promoted from meat and seafood category manager to director of AI strategy and innovation at Springdale-based Harps Food Stores.
Symphony of Northwest Arkansas to open mainstage season on October 3. The Symphony of Northwest Arkansas will begin its mainstage season on October 3 with “Rites of Renewal: The Firebird.”
Yuna nishamura wins NW Arkansas Championship. Yuna Nishamura won the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship presented by P&G, marking her first LPGA victory.
Sheep Dog Impact Assistance takes over Veterans Wall of honor care. Veterans in Bella Vista celebrated a new chapter for the Veterans Wall of Honor as Sheep Dog Impact Assistance assumes responsibility for the memorial's care.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 27, 2026
item.description:
The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
Centerton food pantry closes after 15 years. A Centerton food pantry has closed after 15 years of operation. The pantry distributed over 1.8 million pounds of food to more than 92,000 individuals.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of the ordinance.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider a lot split at 44 Watson Drive. This proposal would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 at 44 Watson Drive into multiple lots, if approved.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve purchasing a new tractor for the Street Department. The city is asked to approve a contract for $63,860.36 to purchase a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for use by the Street Department.
Fayetteville Falltoberfest returns October 4. Fayetteville Falltoberfest will return on October 4, featuring German traditions, local music, art, food, and a dog pageant.
Northwest Arkansas Book Fest held at Walton Arts Center. The fourth annual Northwest Arkansas Book Fest took place at the Walton Arts Center. The event featured a full day of activities for readers of all ages.
Experts suggest diversifying Northwest Arkansas employers for growth. Experts suggest that Northwest Arkansas should diversify its employer base beyond its four major companies to maintain rapid regional growth.
Bikes, Blues & BBQ offers more than just biking events. The CEO of the Rogers-Lowell Chamber stated that Bikes, Blues & BBQ is not exclusively for bikers. The event also offers music and food for attendees.
Arkansas classical theatre presents Poe production. The Arkansas Classical Theatre is returning with a unique production based on the works of Edgar Allan Poe.
Centerton hosts NWA Emergency Preparedness Fair. Centerton hosted the NWA Emergency Preparedness Fair, where residents learned about safety. The event included participation from the Centerton Police Department, Centerton Fire Department, and Mercy Life Health.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 26, 2026
item.description:
The Arkansas Community Foundation launched a new program with a $10 million grant to address food insecurity in the state.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider splitting a lot at 44 Watson Drive. This proposed lot split, Case LSP-2026-67100, would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 into multiple parcels. The applicant is Troy Currens.
Arkansas Community Foundation launches $10 million food insecurity fund. The Arkansas Community Foundation, in cooperation with the Walmart Foundation, announced a five-year initiative to address food insecurity, anchored by a $10 million grant from the Walmart Foundation.
McAuley Place development to welcome first residents in October. The McAuley Place development in Bentonville, which aims to offer affordable living options for teachers, will see its first residents move in next month.
Arkansas Department of Transportation to remove political signs from right-of-ways. The Arkansas Department of Transportation reminded candidates and their supporters that placing campaign signs on highway right-of-ways is unlawful and the department will remove them.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Walmart CEO addresses rumors about digital labels and AI pricing. Walmart CEO John Furner is pushing back on rumors regarding the retail giant's new pricing technology and its use of digital labels and AI.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 25, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
Benton county Quorum court approves fund for ICE program. The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through its 287(g) Program.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of the ordinance.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve purchase of a new tractor for the Street Department. The city is asked to approve a contract for $63,860.36 to purchase a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for use by the Street Department.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve appointment to the bella vista library advisory board. The Mayor's appointment of Julie Driver Grau to the Bella Vista Library Advisory Board would be approved, filling a term ending December 31, 2030.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville school board renames performing arts facility. The Fayetteville School District's Performing Arts Center has been renamed in honor of longtime educator Warren Rosenaur.
Fayetteville park reopens after $1 million in improvements. Bryce Davis Park in Fayetteville reopened after the completion of approximately $1 million in park improvements.
Bentonville's Arkade adds 14 startup businesses. Bentonville's Arkade added 14 startup businesses in its first year.
Bentonville nonprofit advances in NASA challenge. Bentonville-based nonprofit research organization Autonomic Resilience Collective advanced to the final stage of a NASA challenge to design a food system for Mars.
VIC Tech appoints Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer. VIC Technology Venture Development, a Fayetteville-based company, named Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer and managing director.
Heartland Whole health launches rural health initiative. A Northwest Arkansas-based nonprofit, Heartland Whole Health, is starting an initiative to address the gap in healthcare access for millions of Americans in rural areas.
Crystal bridges to host Indigenous Arts symposium. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host an Indigenous Arts Symposium next month, featuring Indigenous artists and scholars.
Siloam Springs 'Twin Springs' landmark undergoing construction. A downtown Siloam Springs landmark, 'Twin Springs,' which has been closed to the public for over two decades, is undergoing renovation.
Fayetteville school construction projects on schedule. Ongoing Fayetteville School District projects, including Woodland Junior High, are expected to be completed on schedule.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 24, 2026
item.description:
Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31.
Brandom Gengelbach to leave Bentonville chamber leadership. Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31, three years after being hired to lead the organization.
Bentonville City Council approves grants for road projects. The Bentonville City Council approved grants to partially fund several planned infrastructure projects in the city.
Bentonville City Council approves new artificial intelligence policy. The Bentonville City Council approved new guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence to comply with Arkansas state law.
UL Solutions expands testing at Lowell Retail Center of Excellence. UL Solutions expanded its Retail Center of Excellence in Lowell to include apparel and textiles testing, adding to its existing testing of furniture, toys, and electronics.
Updates provided on Bentonville overpass projects. A Bentonville City Council meeting included status updates on projects designed to improve traffic movement across Interstate 49.
Combined sales tax revenue up in four Northwest Arkansas cities. Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale reported a combined monthly sales tax revenue of $9.965 million in September, an increase of 2.35%.
Circle of life to acquire Washington Regional Hospice. Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and purchase the Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville.
Pay-what-you-can bookshop reopens in downtown Springdale. A nonprofit pay-what-you-can bookshop reopened in downtown Springdale, allowing readers to take books for free or pay what they can.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Centerton food pantry to close after 15 years. The Centerton Food Pantry will close its doors after serving the community for 15 years.
Proposed waste management merger faces challenges in Benton County. Merger negotiators were informed that combining Northwest Arkansas' two solid waste districts faces an uphill climb in Benton County.
Lasang Pinoy restaurant in Rogers makes 50-best list. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant in Rogers, represents Arkansas on the New York Times' 2026 list of America's Best Restaurants.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 23, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved accepting over $5 million in grants for transportation projects.
Bentonville city council approves accepting over $5 million in transportation grants. The Bentonville City Council approved accepting two grants totaling more than $5 million for transportation projects aimed at enhancing the city's transit infrastructure.
Rogers city council approves Mount hebron road rezoning. The Rogers City Council approved a rezoning for Mount Hebron Road, a decision that followed an earlier denial and left some residents disappointed.
Hotel Vin Rogers opens in Pinnacle Hills. A new hotel, Hotel Vin Rogers, has opened in the Pinnacle Hills area, representing an investment of over $72 million and featuring three food and beverage concepts, an outdoor pool, and more than 10,000 square feet of event space.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
XNA sees narrow dip in August outbound passenger traffic. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) experienced its second year-over-year decrease in outbound passenger traffic in August, following two consecutive months of record-high enplanements.
Crystal Bridges announces $250,000 Don Tyson Prize recipient. Crystal Bridges has announced the recipient of the 2026 Don Tyson Prize for the Advancement of American Art, which awards $250,000.
Boys and Girls Club of Benton County to offer free dinner for children and teens. The Boys and Girls Club of Benton County will provide free dinner and snacks for children aged 6-18 starting next year.
NWA Food Bank receives donation to kick off Walmart NW Arkansas Championship week. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank received a joint donation of $20,000 and 40,000 pounds of protein from Walmart and Tyson Foods to mark the start of the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship.
Centerton run to support foster children on October 10. Schuber Mitchell Homes is bringing the Love Running Home 5K & 1-Mile Fun Run to Centerton on October 10, an event designed to support children in foster care.
Acres.com releases housing market data product. Fayetteville-based land intelligence platform Acres.com has launched a new product that offers a nationwide view of housing market supply, pricing, and demand.
Springdale city council approves AI policy. The Springdale City Council has approved a policy to establish guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence, as mandated by Arkansas state law.
New York Times lists Rogers Filipino restaurant among U.S.' 50 best. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant located at 719 W. Walnut St., Suite 104, in Rogers, was included in The New York Times' recently released list of America's Best Restaurants 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 21, 2026
item.description:
The Siloam Springs city board will consider rezoning 13 acres for a 285-unit apartment development along Arkansas 16 during its October meeting.
Siloam Springs city board to consider rezoning for 285-unit apartment development. The Siloam Springs city Board of Directors is set to consider rezoning about 13 acres along Arkansas 16 to make way for an apartment development during its October meeting.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax residents pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%).
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to amend Ordinance No. 24-04 regarding sewer revenue bond terms. This proposed amendment would revise the terms for the outstanding City of Rogers, Arkansas Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 2024, which could affect the city's financial obligations related to its sewer system.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider approving Resolution 26-25 for a 457(b) Deferred Compensation Plan. This proposed resolution would establish or modify a deferred compensation plan for employees, which could impact their retirement savings.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
University of Arkansas Medical Sciences opens new MS clinic in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences opened a new clinic for MS patients on September 18 in Fayetteville.
Bentonville School District receives highest a-ranking in the state. The Bentonville School District is leading the list of the top school districts in Arkansas with its highest A-ranking.
Arkansas Latinas en Bici hosts community bike ride in Bentonville. Arkansas Latinas en Bici, a local cycle group, hosted a community bike ride event throughout Bentonville on Sunday, September 20, encouraging community members to explore Northwest Arkansas.
UAMS hosts Girlology session for puberty education in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) hosted a 'Girlology' informational session for young girls navigating puberty on Sunday in Fayetteville.
Northwest Arkansas cattle ranch expands operations. The 808 Ranch, located 15 minutes from downtown Bentonville, is expanding its operations and adding technology.
Arkansas basketball SEC-ACC challenge game times announced. The Razorbacks men's team will face North Carolina at 6:30 p.m. Central in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, while the women's team will play Wake Forest at 8 p.m. Central in Fayetteville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 20, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville's City Council and Finance Committee will meet on September 22 to discuss various city matters.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to decrease the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). This change would mean residents pay less tax on prepared food and beverage purchases.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to accept a $185,605 grant for the John DeShields Trail design and bidding. This would fund the design and bidding documents for trail improvements along the John DeShields Trail corridor between NE J Street and E Central Avenue.
Northwest Arkansas National Airport shelves hotel and convenience store plans. Plans for a hotel and convenience store at Northwest Arkansas National Airport are on hold due to low developer interest and high interest rates.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026.
Maple Leaf acquires don's Canopies. Maple Leaf has completed the acquisition of Don's Canopies, as reported in the Northwest Arkansas business briefs.
Springdale's East Emma Avenue streetscape project to begin in October. A $4.8 million project to improve East Emma Avenue in Springdale is expected to commence at the beginning of October.
Harps Food Stores announces director promotions. Harps Food Stores Inc. has promoted William Haulmark to director of insurance and Will McDoniel to director of AI strategy and innovation.
Grandma Moses exhibition opens at Crystal Bridges. The "Grandma Moses: A Good Day's Work" exhibition, featuring nearly 150 works, has opened at Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville.
Bentonville hosts Clean the Streets Day. The City of Bentonville held a city-wide "Clean the Streets Day" on Saturday, participating in Keep America Beautiful's Great Arkansas Cleanup.
LPGA 5K race returns to Bentonville for Mercy Hospital. The LPGA 5K race returned to Bentonville on Saturday, benefiting Mercy Hospital and including community exercise and the Annual Corporate Challenge.
Benton County holds annual Passport Saturday event. The Benton County Circuit Clerk's Office hosted its annual Passport Saturday event, allowing residents to apply for passports.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 19, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville and Bella Vista city councils will consider various proposals this week.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). This change would mean residents pay less tax on restaurant meals and other prepared food items.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept $4,000,000.00 in grant funds for Greenhouse Road Improvements. Accepting these grant funds would help pay for construction of improvements on Greenhouse Road between Hwy 12 and Hwy 102, with the city contributing 55% of a $1,000,000.00 local match.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 18, 2026
item.description:
A $700 million AWSOM Whole Health Campus broke ground in Northwest Arkansas.
AWSOM Whole Health Campus breaks ground for $700 million facility. A groundbreaking ceremony was held for the $700 million AWSOM Whole Health Campus, bringing specialty healthcare to Northwest Arkansas.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). If approved, this would mean a lower tax on meals and drinks purchased in the city.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than currently permitted for single-family homes. The Planning Commission recommended approval with a 7-0 vote.
On the Bentonville Construction Board of Appeals agenda: Board to hear appeal from Burckart Construction. Burckart Construction is appealing a decision made by the Building Fire and Safety department. The board will decide whether to uphold or overturn that decision.
Pea Ridge sidewalk project delayed by protected bats. A sidewalk project along McCulloch Street in Pea Ridge has been stalled due to the presence of protected bats.
Walmart pilots health ambassador program in rural stores. Walmart is testing a health ambassador program in rural stores to explore how pharmacists can provide more personalized health guidance to customers.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Best friends pet resource center and centerton animal services offer adventure buddies day. Best Friends Pet Resource Center and Centerton Animal Services will offer adoptable dogs for fun outings as part of Adventure Buddies Day, a nationwide initiative.
Rogers Public Schools Superintendent Jeff Perry to retire. Rogers Public Schools Superintendent Jeff Perry announced his retirement at the end of the current school year.
University of Arkansas, Fayetteville reports record high graduation rates. The University of Arkansas, Fayetteville is reporting record high four-year and six-year graduation rates.
Northwest Technical Institute reports rising enrollment. Northwest Technical Institute has reported increased interest across many of its skilled trades programs for the fall semester.
Retail experts discuss AI and customer needs in Bentonville. Executives from Walmart Inc., Google LLC, and the National Retail Federation, along with consumer experts, discussed the future of retail and the importance of customer trust.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 17, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville closed a downtown parking lot to begin construction on a new parking garage for Dave Peel Park.
Bentonville closes downtown parking lot for Dave Peel Park garage. Bentonville closed its 110-space public parking lot at 300 E. Central Ave. to make way for a new parking garage. The garage is part of the Dave Peel Park expansion and will add 283 public spaces.
Bentonville Health Care Campus hosts groundbreaking ceremony. Leaders from the Alice L. Walton Foundation, Mercy Health, and the community broke ground on the new Bentonville Health Care Campus.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to discuss ongoing collaboration with NWACC. This item is a continuation of previous discussions regarding the partnership between the Public Art Advisory Board and Northwest Arkansas Community College.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider a construction Manager/General contractor (CM/GC) contract for RPCF improvements. This contract would establish an agreement for a construction manager and general contractor to oversee and perform improvements at the Rogers Pollution Control Facility.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Board to review updates on the 2027 Project Plan. This item will provide residents with information on the progress of public art projects planned for 2027.
Peel Compton Foundation names new Bentonville property Central House & Gardens. The Peel Compton Foundation officially named its newest property at 606 Central Avenue as the Central House & Gardens.
Bentonville schools reports increased student enrollment for 2026-27. The Bentonville School Board approved the district's 2026-27 fiscal year budget and noted that the district's enrollment is increasing, contrary to statewide trends.
Aerospace and defense summit held at The Ledger. The Arkansas Aerospace and Defense Alliance's Mid-America Aerospace and Defense Summit took place at The Ledger in Bentonville on August 25-26. The event drew over 300 attendees from approximately 100 companies, government agencies, and universities.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. It is part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Cox customers convert to Spectrum brand. Former Cox customers in Arkansas will see new branding on their bills and service interactions as the integration with Spectrum began on September 16.
J.B. Hunt expects higher costs to reduce Q3 earnings. Lowell-based J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. expects its third-quarter earnings to fall 5% to 10% from the second quarter due to higher costs.
Crafton Tull promotes Daniel Ellis to chief operating officer. Rogers-based engineering and design firm Crafton Tull promoted Daniel Ellis to chief operating officer.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 16, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans to convert the former home of James "Bud" Walton into a botanical garden.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves botanical garden for Bud Walton home. The Bentonville Planning Commission approved plans to transform a home previously owned by James "Bud" Walton into a new public attraction.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Discussing the NWACC Collaboration. The board will continue discussions on the collaboration with Northwest Arkansas Community College.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider a construction Manager/General contractor contract for Rogers Pollution Control Facility improvements. The Commission is asked to approve a contract for a Construction Manager/General Contractor to oversee improvements at the Rogers Pollution Control Facility.
On the Bentonville Public Art Advisory Board agenda: Reviewing the 2027 Project Plan. The board will receive updates on the progress of the 2027 Project Plan.
UAMS opens telehealth booth at Northwest Arkansas National Airport. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences Northwest Regional Campus installed a new telehealth booth at Northwest Arkansas National Airport, offering virtual healthcare access to travelers and staff.
Walmart to test health ambassador program in rural stores. Walmart will test a health ambassador role as part of its ongoing efforts to expand its healthcare business, which includes store pharmacists and telehealth options.
Amazeum expansion to open in November. The Amazeum, a children's museum in Northwest Arkansas, is set to open an expansion in November.
Rogers Superintendent Jeff Perry to exit next June. Superintendent Jeff Perry announced his plans to conclude his tenure with Rogers Public Schools in June.
Fayetteville Animal Services advisory board proposes new shelter location. The Fayetteville Animal Services Advisory Board discussed a potential location for a future animal services facility to present to the city council.
Raising cane's considers replacing Fayetteville location. A Fayetteville Raising Cane's restaurant may relocate, though the planning commission recently voted against approving a permit for a potential new site.
Fayetteville parks to host three ribbon-cuttings for new projects. The Fayetteville Parks and Recreation Department has scheduled multiple ribbon-cutting events in the coming months for completed projects, including a new park.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville City Council discusses aquatic center site selection. The Fayetteville City Council held a nearly two-hour discussion regarding the next steps in selecting a site for the aquatic center approved in a recent bond election.
Lowell leaders discuss Flock Safety system but delay changes. A proposed resolution to ban the use of Flock Safety systems in Lowell led to a lengthy discussion among City Council members, but no vote was taken.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 15, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville is seeking applicants to fill vacancies on multiple city boards.
Bentonville seeks applicants for city boards. The city of Bentonville is looking for applicants to fill vacancies on three municipal boards.
Bentonville Planning Commission to consider botanical garden site plan. The Bentonville Planning Commission will consider a site plan for a botanical garden on the former property of an original Walmart executive.
Bentonville warns drivers of Southwest Fourth Street closure. The city of Bentonville is advising drivers of a three-day closure of Southwest Fourth Street this month for sewer tap installation.
Northwest Arkansas Community College receives $680,000 for outdoor recreation spaces. Northwest Arkansas Community College plans to use a $680,000 grant to develop new trails and outdoor recreation spaces on campus.
Harps Food announces CEO transition in early 2027. Springdale-based Harps Food Stores has named J. Max Van Hoose to succeed Kim Eskew, who will step down as CEO and chairman in early 2027.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority in the amount of $9,621,360.00, with $887,911.00 of that amount being a principal forgiveness bond.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 201 SW E Street from allowing only suburban single-family homes to a 'Neighborhood Edge' designation, which typically permits a wider variety of housing types and mixed uses.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to review financial reports. This is a routine update on the financial status of Rogers Water Utilities.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet on September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education is scheduled to hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, call to order, pledge, roll call, and approval or modification of the agenda.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority in the amount of $9,621,360.00, with $887,911.00 of that principal amount in the form of a principal forgiveness bond.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 201 SW E Street from allowing only suburban single-family homes to a 'Neighborhood Edge' designation, which typically permits a wider variety of housing types and mixed uses.
On the Bella Vista Board of Zoning Adjustment agenda: Board to consider a variance for a non-residential structure at 19 Cheviot Place. This would allow a detached nonresidential structure at 19 Cheviot Place to be placed differently than current rules allow. This could affect the appearance or use of the property.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place on October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
Bat discovery delays Pea Ridge sidewalk construction. Construction of a sidewalk on McCulloch Street in Pea Ridge is facing delays due to the discovery of bats living in nearby trees.
Pea Ridge leaders plan to preserve Rich family homestead. Pea Ridge leaders are developing plans for a natural park on the property of the former Rich family homestead. Mayor Nathan See aims to preserve the natural setting of the historic site.
Fayetteville City Council to consider vendor for Lake Fayetteville marina shop. The Fayetteville City Council is scheduled to vote on the approval of a new vendor for the Lake Fayetteville marina rental and concession shop. The space has been vacant for approximately nine months.
Fayetteville City Council to consider aquatic center site study funding. The Fayetteville City Council is expected to consider allocating up to $75,000 for an additional assessment of potential site locations for the aquatic center. The aquatic center was approved as part of this year's bond package.
Springdale Fire chief discusses new station for city growth. The Springdale Fire Chief stated that a new fire station is intended to help the department keep pace with the city's growth in residents and expanding city limits.
Simmons Foods CEO discusses generational perspective. Todd Simmons, CEO of Simmons Foods, expressed his focus on a 'generational perspective' in his role. He has been CEO for over a decade.
Washington Regional hires new physicians. Fayetteville-based Washington Regional has announced new physician hires. Rogers-based Generations Bank also announced new hires and promotions.
Springdale hosts annual Squirrel Cook-off. The annual World Champion Squirrel Cook-off returned to Springdale on Saturday. The event featured various squirrel-based dishes.
Nonprofit builds beds for Northwest Arkansas children. A local nonprofit chapter constructed 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas. The organization aims to ensure that no children in the area sleep on the floor.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 13, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will meet on September 15, 2026, to approve its agenda and recognize individuals.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education will hold a meeting on September 15, 2026, at 5:30 PM at the Administration Building. The agenda includes a welcome, roll call, approval of the agenda, and recognitions.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11 in Bentonville. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the larger Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to finance a portion of the 48" Supply Water Transmission Project. This resolution would allow the city to finance a portion of a large water transmission project with bonds purchased by the Arkansas Development Finance Authority, including a principal forgiveness bond of $887,911.00.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 201 SW E Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge.. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street, moving from single-family homes to a neighborhood edge style within a walkable neighborhood.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider requiring 200-foot distance between short-term rentals in residential zones. This proposal would mean that new short-term rentals in residential areas would need to be at least 200 feet away from any existing short-term rental. This could affect where new short-term rental properties can be established in the city.
Centerton's downtown master plan requires public-private partnerships. Centerton officials state that the city's Downtown Master Plan will necessitate public-private partnerships for its revitalization and expansion. The city is currently determining the next steps after about a year of planning.
Colliers Arkansas announces additions and promotion to Northwest Arkansas team. Colliers Arkansas has announced four new additions and one promotion to its Northwest Arkansas team. The team is based in Rogers at 3503 S. 55th St., Suite 200.
GoodWorks hosts inaugural Day of service with 14 nonprofits. GoodWorks, a volunteer center of the Jones Center, hosted its first Day of Service on Saturday. The event connected residents with 14 local nonprofits to support volunteerism across Northwest Arkansas.
Volunteers build 250 beds for Northwest Arkansas children. Volunteers in Bentonville built 250 beds for children in Northwest Arkansas as part of the annual Bunks Across America event by Sleep in Heavenly Peace. This initiative aims to provide beds for children who need them.
XNA transitions from zero security to modern TSA standards. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) has evolved from having no security to implementing modern Transportation Security Administration (TSA) standards. This change reflects the normalization of security procedures for travelers.
Concerns raised about ICE operations' impact on Northwest Arkansas businesses. Irma Chavez, founder of the Arkansas Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, has expressed concerns about the impact of nationwide enhanced immigration enforcement on Northwest Arkansas businesses. She noted that small and family-owned businesses are particularly vulnerable.
Northwest Arkansas Food Bank and cystic fibrosis foundation hold fundraising events. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank held its second annual Flavor of Giving fundraiser on August 27 at Osage House in Cave Springs. The Cystic Fibrosis Foundation also hosted an event to raise funds for local causes.
Erik Dees releases new book on values-driven leadership. Erik Dees, a partner at Fayetteville-based Milestone Leadership, has released a new book titled "Keeper of the Culture." The book challenges leaders to redefine success and what constitutes strong leadership.
